lede: Plants respond to their surroundings by growing rather than moving. A shoot lit from one side grows more on the shaded side and so bends towards the light, and the hormone auxin, made at the tip, is what makes that happen.
can: Name phototropism and auxin, and say where auxin is made.
Explain the bend as uneven auxin and cell elongation.
Read the tip experiments and say what each treatment shows.

md: A seedling on a windowsill leans towards the glass within a day or two. It is not turning; one side has simply grown longer than the other, because a hormone made in the tip collects on the shaded side and stretches the cells there.

title: The four words that carry the marks
md:
**Phototropism** — the growth response of a stem towards light.
**Auxin** — the plant hormone that causes it.
**Uneven distribution** — more auxin on the shaded side than the lit side.
**Elongation** — auxin makes cells get *longer*, not more numerous.

prompt: The growth of a shoot towards light is called ______.
explain: Phototropism. Photo- is light and -tropism is a growth response, so the word already tells you what it means. Photosynthesis is a different process entirely, and Summer 2025 examiners saw it offered here.

md: **A tropism is a growth response, not a movement.** The shoot does not swing round like a head turning. Cells on one side get **permanently longer** than cells on the other, and a rod that is longer down one side has to curve. That is what CCEA means by **differential growth**: growth that is different on the two sides.

prompt: A tropism is a growth response. What does that mean for the shoot?
options: cells on one side grow permanently longer
the shoot swings round like a head turning
the shoot slides towards the window
answer: cells on one side grow permanently longer
explain: Differential growth. The curve stays because the cells themselves are longer.

title: Why does more auxin end up on the shaded side?
md: Auxin is made in the **tip**, and light moving across the tip pushes it sideways: it accumulates on the side **away from** the light. It then travels down the shoot on that side. So the shaded side has more auxin, more elongation, more length — and the shoot leans over towards the light. Written the other way round it is worth nothing, so fix the direction now: **more auxin where there is less light**.

prompt: A shoot is lit from the left. On which side is there more auxin?
options: the right side, away from the light
the left side, facing the light
answer: the right side, away from the light
explain: The shaded side — here the right. That side then elongates more and the shoot leans to the left, towards the light.

title: GCSE Biology - Plant Hormones - Tropisms & Auxins
why: Six minutes on auxin and tropisms with the tip experiments drawn out. It also covers gravitropism in roots, which CCEA does not ask for — watch it for the shoot, then answer the question underneath.

prompt: Where in the shoot is auxin produced?
explain: At the tip. That single fact is what makes every tip experiment work: cut the tip off and there is no auxin, so there is no elongation and no bending.

caption: Change one thing at a time and the tip gives itself away.

md: Read the five results as a set. **A** is the control: a whole shoot curves by a mean of **31°**. **B**, with the tip removed, does not curve — and does not grow either. **C**, with the tip covered by a black cap, does not curve: the tip cannot detect the light. **D** proves it is the light and not the cap that matters, because a clear cap leaves the curvature at **30°**. **E** covers the stem *below* the tip and still curves by **32°**, which shows the **tip** is the part that detects light.

prompt: Shoot B had its tip cut off. What happened to it?
options: it did not curve, and it did not grow
it grew faster than the others
answer: it did not curve, and it did not grow
explain: No tip means no auxin, so no elongation — and that means no growth as well as no bend.

title: Summer 2025 B1 Higher Q4 — the answer that stops one word early
md: Candidates were asked what happened to a shoot with no tip. **Most said the tip was missing, so no auxin was present; fewer said there was no growth.** The mark scheme wanted the consequence, not just the cause. The same paper's part (a) asked for arrows on the diagrams, and while most placed the arrow correctly for the first experiment, **fewer did for the second**, and in the third **many did not draw the covering on the shoot tips at all**. If a question gives you a diagram to complete, complete every part of it.

prompt: Shoot C had a black cap over its tip. Its three angles of curvature were 1°, 0°, 2°. What is the mean, in degrees?
explain: (1 + 0 + 2) ÷ 3 = 1°. Type the brackets into the calculator, or the division happens before the addition and the answer falls outside the range of your readings.

prompt: This tree has open sky on one side and dense woodland on the other. Name the response shown, and state which side of each young shoot had the longer cells as the tree grew.

md:
Name **phototropism** and the hormone **auxin**.
Say where auxin is made and which side it collects on.
Explain the bend as **uneven distribution** and cell **elongation**.
Read the tip experiments and say what each one shows.
Give the direction the shoot bends, not just that it moves.

Foundation asks you to name the process, name the hormone and say which way the shoot bends, and that last one wants a direction rather than a feeling. Higher adds the four-step mechanism, often inside a tip experiment with treatments to compare. The first mark is nearly always the hormone; the last is nearly always **elongation**.

title: Not on this specification
md: CCEA's Double Award B1 asks only about **phototropism in stems**. You do **not** need gravitropism (geotropism) in roots, hydrotropism, the commercial uses of plant hormones as weedkillers or rooting powders, gibberellin, ethene, or the names of any experimenters. If a video covers them, enjoy them, but do not spend revision time there.
